locator.text: Display 127.1, p. 127, in the proof of Lemma A.1

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The displayed multilinear (Andreief-type) expansion of det B as an m-fold integral over I_1×⋯×I_m of det[x_j^{α_i}] ∏_j β_j(x_j) is not in the Lean sources; neither is the paper's sign claim that det[x_j^{α_i}] has constant sign on the ordered set {0 < x_1 < ⋯ < x_m} (only its nonvanishing is stated, at powerEvaluationMatrix_det_ne_zero, PowerMomentMatrix.lean:143). The Lean reaches the display's conclusion det B ≠ 0 by a different route: bumpMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero (line 261) rewrites B as intervalMomentMatrix against the measures volume.withDensity β_j and invokes intervalMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero (line 216), which argues by vecMul-injectivity — a column combination c with Bᵗc = 0 makes ∫ powerSum a c dμ_j = 0 for each j, so an averaging/intermediate-value lemma (exists_zero_of_setIntegral_eq_zero, line 158) yields a zero x_j ∈ I_j, the x_j are strictly ordered by interval separation, and powerEvaluationMatrix_det_ne_zero plus the Rolle induction expSum_coefficients_zero (line 74) force c = 0. So the paper's formula as written was not checked; the statement it is used to establish (invertibility of B, Lemma A.1) is stated and proved. Matrix orientation matches the paper: Lean's entry i j is ∫ t^{a i} β j t, i.e. B_{ij} = ∫ x^{α_i} β_j(x) dx.
